sections.report:
**Section.** The whole piece: applies.

**Findings**
1. **Is the copy finished, with no placeholder text and no spelling mistakes?** There is a section heading with nothing under it. "Fares and cards" (x 120–303, y≈548–572) sits over its rule at y≈585, and below it the image is blank to the bottom edge at y 800. A passenger who goes looking for prices or season-card details finds the heading and then nothing. Fares are the one thing on a page like this that a reader acts on and holds the operator to. The blank band could be content that hadn't loaded when the screenshot was taken, or a page cut off at the fold. If either is true this is not a finding, and that should be checked in a live browser. As captured, though, the page promises a section it doesn't deliver. Fix: fill the section with the actual fares and card terms, or remove the heading until they exist. Defect (common sense, since no catalog entry covers this). Weight: major.
2. **Does each heading name what its section holds?** The title, "Winter timetable at the harbour" (x 120–714, y≈60–100), promises a timetable. The page has no sailing times: no departures, no last boat, only "every ninety minutes" and "opens at seven". A reader who came for a timetable scans both columns for times, doesn't find them, and is left to work out departures from "every ninety minutes" with no first sailing given. Also, the six paragraphs above "Fares and cards" (y≈135–510) have no heading, so "Fares and cards" is the only section that gets one. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.6 asks headings to describe the topic of their section. Fix: either add the timetable the title promises (first and last sailings, then every 90 minutes), or retitle the page for what it actually is, such as winter passenger information. Give the opening block its own heading (for example, hours and crossings) so the sections follow one pattern. Defect. Weight: major.
3. **Does every element, rule, box, and ornament do a job, so that removing it would lose something?** There's a second hairline rule in the right column (x 680–1160, y≈585) with no heading above it and nothing below. It looks like the right half of a section rule broken by the column gap, but it reads as the underline of a missing heading. The viewer is left wondering whether a second section is missing. Fix: run the "Fares and cards" rule across the full measure as one line, or drop the right-hand segment. Convention (Tufte, Lupton: rules that carry no information compete with the content). Weight: minor.

**What's working.**
- Type, colour and spacing share one quiet register: a bookish serif in dark grey on white, pale rules, no decoration. That suits a small harbour notice and makes the page feel trustworthy and calm, not promotional.
- The plain, specific copy ("Dogs on a lead are welcome on every sailing", "a rough one closer to thirty-five") answers real passenger questions in a person's voice. It does more for the page than any visual treatment would.

**Couldn't judge from a still.**
- Whether the empty band below "Fares and cards" is the design or content that hadn't loaded or was cut off at the fold. Check the live page and scroll below the fold.

**Checklist.** The whole piece: 8 lines, 5 yes, 3 no (copy finished; each heading names its section; every element does a job).

Walk (working notes):

First read: the eye lands on the bold serif title "Winter timetable at the harbour". It then drops into the left column of body text, moves across to the right column, and ends on "Fares and cards" with a rule under it. There is a matching rule under the right column with no heading above it, and nothing appears below either rule. It reads as an information page for a ferry service, aimed at passengers. The tone is calm and editorial. Job (assumed): to tell passengers how the winter service runs, and let them find sections such as fares quickly.

What matters first:
- One element dominates: **yes**. The title, about 40 px bold, is the clear starting point.
- Each text level distinct, no near-same sizes: **yes**. There are three levels: title (~40 px bold), section heading (~24 px bold), body (~18 px regular). The steps between them are large.
- Headings differ by more than size: **yes**. Both heading levels are bold and dark, and the body is regular.

No line came out `no` or `unsure`, so I had no entries to open.

**Section.** What matters first: applies.

**Findings**
None.

**What's working.**
- **One clear starting point.** The title (y≈60–100, x 120–714) is the only large, heavy element on the page. Nothing competes with it, so the eye knows where to start.
- **Three type levels with big steps between them.** The title is about 40 px bold, "Fares and cards" (y≈548–572) about 24 px bold, and the body about 18 px regular. Each step changes both size and weight, so the section heading stands out from the paragraphs right away and can't be mistaken for the title. Keep these three sizes. Don't add a fourth that sits close to any of them.

**Couldn't judge from a still.**
- Nothing is visible below the rules at y≈585, and the right-hand rule (x 680–1160) has no heading above it. Either the section's content hasn't loaded or the screenshot cut it off. This affects hierarchy only if the right column is meant to have a heading of its own: then the "Fares and cards" level is missing one heading. Check the live page to see what sits under both rules.

**Checklist.** What matters first: 3 lines, 3 yes, 0 no, 0 unsure

**Section.** Arrangement and space: applies.

**Findings**
1. **Do only related elements look alike, with no accidental groups or shapes formed between unrelated ones?** No. Under the right column, at about x 680–1160 and y≈585, there is a grey rule with no heading above it. It matches the rule under "Fares and cards" (x 120–600) in weight, colour and height. The viewer reads it as the second half of a pair: a heading that should be there and isn't, or a broken page. Their eye goes to the empty right side looking for a section title. The likely cause is one of two. Either a full-width section divider was split by the column grid, or the section heading was put into a two-column cell and only one cell was filled. Look-alikes read as a group, so a matching rule with nothing above it makes a group that doesn't exist (Wertheimer; Arnheim, *Art and Visual Perception*, ch. II). Fix: make the section heading and its rule span the full measure (x 120–1160) as one unbroken element. If the rule is meant to belong to "Fares and cards" alone, drop the right-hand one. Defect. Weight: minor. It doesn't stop anyone reading the timetable, but it makes the page look broken just where a new section starts.

**What's working.**
- The two-column grid is strict and repeats. There are two equal columns (about 120–600 and 680–1160) with one 80 px gutter. The headline, the "Fares and cards" heading and both text columns all hang from the same left edges, so nothing looks placed by eye. Keep this grid when the fares content is added.
- Lines in the two columns sit on the same baselines. Both start at y≈145, share one leading and one paragraph gap, so the first lines (145, 172, 199…) and the paragraph breaks line up across the gutter. The spread reads as one calm block, not two drifting ones. The spacing also shows the groups: lines within a paragraph sit closer than paragraphs, and there is a clearly bigger gap (about 45 px) above "Fares and cards" than between the heading and its rule. So the heading belongs to what follows it.

**Couldn't judge from a still.**
- The "Fares and cards" section ends at its rule with nothing below it, and about 210 px of blank page follows (y≈590–800). This may be a capture cut off mid-page or content that never loaded, rather than the design. Check in a live browser that the fares content appears under the heading. If the section really is empty, the heading leads into nothing and needs content or removing.
- I couldn't check how the two columns reflow on a narrow screen, including where the orphan rule ends up.

**Checklist.** Arrangement and space: 13 lines, 12 yes, 1 no (no accidental groups: the matching rule with no heading under the right column at y≈585), 0 unsure.

**Section.** Text: applies.

**Findings**
1. **Do paragraphs and columns break cleanly, with no lone short word on a last line and no heading at the foot of a column?** The worst case is the "Fares and cards" heading at about (120, 545–585). It sits at the bottom of the text with its rule under it, and no text follows it, either below it or at the top of a next column. The rule opposite it at (680–1160, 585) has no heading at all. A reader who looks for fares finds only a label and an empty space, so it reads as content that failed to load or was left out. Fix: keep a heading together with at least its first lines of text, or move it to the top of the next column or page. If this space really is empty, fill it or remove the heading and both rules. Bringhurst does not state the heading-at-foot rule, so this is common sense. Defect. Weight: major, because fares are one of the things a passenger came for and this heading promises them and gives nothing.
2. **Same line, smaller cases:** In the right column, "bags." sits alone on the last line of the bicycles paragraph at about (680, 375), and "thirty-five." sits alone on the last line of the crossings paragraph at about (680, 253). Both are short words alone on a last line and leave a ragged gap. Fix: re-break or edit the copy slightly so at least two words carry over (Bringhurst, *The Elements of Typographic Style*, 2.4.2). Convention. Weight: minor.

**What's working.**
- The body text is set well for reading. It's a plain serif at a comfortable size, dark on white. Lines run about 55–60 characters, within 45–75, and the line spacing is generous. Both columns read without effort.
- The paragraphs are short, separated by space without indents, and set flush left with a soft rag. The text comes in easy pieces.

**Couldn't judge from a still.** I couldn't tell if the empty area below "Fares and cards" is the design or a page caught mid-load or cut off by the screenshot. Check it in a live browser. Either way, the heading with nothing under it is what the viewer sees here.

**Checklist.** Text: 30 lines, 29 yes, 1 no (paragraphs and columns break cleanly)
